Under the bill as originally introduced into this house it required the approval of the governor in council both for the authorization of the superintendent of pilots to exercise any of the pilotage authority functions, and for the special authorization in connection with any particular power. Under the proposed amendment the pilotage authority, which may be the minister, the deputy minister, or the acting minister, or the superintendent of pilots, may authorize any one of his functions to be performed for such time or such purpose as he may decide without the deterrent of having that authorization given the approval of the governor in council. Is that not a distinct difference?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: I think, Mr. Chairman, that it must be done by by-law approved by the governor in council.

Not according to the
amendment now before us.
Better to leave things as they are.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext:
The amendment reads:
Whenever the minister is appointed as pilotage authority for any district, his successors in office or any acting minister or, in the absence of the minister, his lawful deputy, shall be the pilotage authority, and any such pilotage authority may by by-law confirmed by the governor in council, authorize the superintendent of pilots in the district to exercise any of his functions.
Then follows the clause to which I referred.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext:
It continues:
Moreover, such pilotage authority may, foi such time or such purpose as he may decide, authorize any person to exercise any particular function or power vested in the pilotage authority by this act or any by-law made hereunder.
I think everything should be done by bylaw ratified by order in council.

But not as it reads. My point is that the pilotage authority may authorize the exercise by any person of any of his powers under this act without the sanction of any by-law and without the approval of the governor in council, as the last clause now reads. In the original amendment the approval of the governor in council is made a condition precedent both to the appointment of a superintendent of pilots to exercise the powers of the pilotage authority, and to authorizing the delegation by the pilotage authority to anyone else of his functions in any particular case. But in the amendment now before us the approval of the governor in council is not necessary. The pilotage authority may delegate his power without reference to the governor in council or without any by-law, for such time or such purpose as he may decide.
The last clause referred to a particular function.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: This amendment was suggested by the pilots themselves after consultation with the Department of Justice, but if my hon. friends think there is a doubt as to the meaning of the amendment I have no objection to adding a word or two to make it clear. We might delete the words between the word "functions" in the eighth line of the typewritten amendment and the word "for" in the next line, and insert after the word "functions" the word "and".

Is there any other difference in the amendment except that the absence of the minister is a condition required before his deputy can exercise his powers? If, not why not simplify it by adding after the words "his stead and" on the twelfth line the words "in his absence." The section appears to me to be admirably drafted.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: Objection was taken as to the wording of certain parts of the draft. The words "without more," for instance, were objected to by someone yesterday.

That is all right; the words "without more" are necessary; the authority goes without anything further thar the act itself.
Canada Shipping Act
Mr. Chairman, I put a question, just now, to the hon. minister. I wish to know whether sections 395 and 397 will have the same effeot as they had previously, when this amendment is adopted?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, the section which we intend to amend does not only affect the pilotage of Quebec, Montreal, Halifax and Vancouver, it affects all pilots who come under the jurisdiction of the Minister of Marine, so that there will be no discrimination between pilots of Quebec and Montreal or other parts of Canada. May I add that the amendment such as proposed, after the changes suggested by my hon. friend are made, meet all the needs of the situation; it is perfectly clear and I submit it should be accepted.
The minister spoke about pilots having been consulted concerning this amendment. Does he mean pilots of Quebec and Montreal? Have the pilots of Halifax and Vancouver been consulted?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: The pilots generally.
Representatives of pilots generally.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: I believe I have not understood my hon. friend correctly. I do not believe the pilots of Halifax and Vancouver were consulted. This amendment was asked for by officials of the department. Pilots of Montreal I understand objected to the wording of the amendment, and suggested the substitution of the amendment which was just proposed.

As I understand it the amendment is suggested because of the fact that in some cases it is found necessary for the pilotage authority actually to be in attendance at the port. Would the minister tell me what those cases would be?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext:
Let us consider subsection (j) of the general powers of pilotage authorities contained in section 415 of the act:
(j) provide for the compulsory retirement of licensed pilots who have not attained the age of sixty-five years, proved on oath before the pilotage authority ito be incapacitated by mental or bodily infirmity or by habits of drunkenness.
If proof has to be taken in Halifax and Vancouver, under the law as it stands to-day the minister would have to go there to take such evidence.
Mr, RALSTON: Or they would have to come here?
[Mr. Bury.l
Mr. DURANlLEAU: Yes, or they would have to come here. Therefore we want to delegate the power to someone else so that such person could take the oath.
Why not let Mahomet come to the mountain?
It may cost a lot of money.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: I do not think the amendment means much, because it is effective only in the absence of the minister. And as stated a moment ago by the hon. member for St. Henri surely the deputy minister must have some authority in the department. There are other duties performed by the deputy minister in the absence of the minister.
And more important duties.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: The minister is always head of the department, and on his return he could make a change in the decision made by the deputy minister.
It is only a delegation of power in some special instances.

Mr. Chairman, I have received a telegram from the Pilot Association of Quebec strongly protesting against this amendment being enacted. As I stated at the outset of my remarks, when the explanatory note states that the amendment only affects the pilots of Halifax and Vancouver, it is clear that this was intended to deceive us. It is as follows:
These provisions which are new, is to avoid the necessity of actual attendance of the minister as pilotage authority, possibly at Halifax or Vancouver . . .
It is because they are the most remote points.

In truth, it looks as if the amendment was aimed at the Quebec and Montreal pilots. However, sections 395 and 397 remain in the Act, thereby liable to stir trouble. In the future, if the Quebec pilots refuse to conform themselves to an order received from the pilotage authority, they may base their contentions on section 395 which stipulates that they are still under the authority of the Minister of Marine Who will decide whether section 395 or section 414, as amended, should apply? I submit that there is ambiguity and had the intention been to only include the pilots of Halifax and Vancouver, it should be so stipulated in the amendment.

The cities of Halifax and Vancouver were mentioned because they were extreme points which the minister could not reach. In such instances he would delegate his power.

Canada Shipping Act
It is stated " possibly."
The amendment applies to the sections you have just quoted, because it is stipulated that when the minister is appointed as pilotage authority, his powers may be delegated. That applies to your case.
Notwithstanding what the hon. member for Richelieu (Mr. Cardin) may think, from the legal aspect, section 395 still will provide that the minister constitutes the pilotage authority.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext:
The
minister or his deputy.

My concern is this: While apparently the amendment is for the benefit of the harbours of Quebec and Montreal, they really do not need the amendment because the minister could attend at those points. It seems to me that in effect the amendment will apply only to the points far away. If there is any benefit in having the act as it was before, with the minister acting as pilotage authority, it does not seem to me that those points should be deprived of a benefit simply because other points happened to be nearer. I am in accord with the idea of delegating authority to a certain extent in special cases. But this amendment goes much further by way of delegation than is usually the case. As a rule the term "minister" includes an acting minister. The present amendment, however, goes further and provides for the "deputy minister," and then there is further provision "in the absence of the minister." As a matter of fact there is usually an acting minister, if the minister is absent any length of time. It seems to me that that should cover the case, rather than have a further delegation not only to the deputy but to someone else altogether, namely the superintendent of pilots. Then from the superintendent of pilots it goes to someone else. I submit this is delegation with a vengeance.
Everything is done by bylaw.

I am showing that the delegation is not done by by-law. The delegation is done simply by someone writing a letter. In any other function of the minister you do not have the minister delegating his power; the acting minister always has power. Sometimes the deputy minister has power, but you do not have a further delegation to the superintendent of pilots, then to some
other official, and then from him to somebody else. It seems to me we are making the section more involved than is necessary. As pilots from outside points have not been consulted, there may be some objections. I do not know whether or not there could be, but if there was any benefit in having the act as it stood before and as it has been for many years, why change it just at this time, and have all these powers of delegation?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: The hon. member has stated that the proposed amendment may be useful in outside districts such as Halifax and Vancouver, but that perhaps it may not be necessary at other points because the minister could go to Quebec and perform his pilotage duties. However if there were an inquiry held even at Quebec I should hesitate to go myself. In some circumstances I believe it would be proper to delegate powers to hold an inquiry even in Quebec, instead of forcing the minister to leave his office for that purpose.
Would the minister tell me how many pilotage districts there are in Nova Scotia? Sheet Harbour used to be a pilotage district, but I do not know whether it is now or not.	*

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: There are two, Halifax and Sydney.
Under the minister.

Mr. Chairman, I still maintain my contentions in connection with the amendment proposed. Last year, an official of the department, Captain Robertson, on his own responsibility, suspended seven pilots. A number of pilots having refused to undertake some special service, those who had made the request immediately communicated with Ottawa. At the time, the hon. Minister of Marine was absent What happened? Captain Robertson, on his own authority, suspended six or seven pilots, by telegram. These Quebec pilots were suspended because they had refused to undertake some special service, notwithstanding the fact that such pilotage authority was not vested in the superintendent. Not only he had not that authority but he was unaware of the provisions of a contract between the shipping federation and the Quebec Pilots' Union. If that authority is vested in the superintendent, the same thing will happen as last year, he will suspend without any cause these pilots. I again contend that the authority to appoint pilots and fix pilotage rates should not be vested in officials of the:
Canada Shipping Act

department, but that this authority should be left with the minister or, perhaps, the deputy minister and no other official.

Could the hon. member for Quebec-Mont-morency (Mr. Dorion) inform the house as to what happened to -these seven pilots? I understand -they were suspended in virtue of the authority delegated by the minister?

No, they
were not suspended under authority delegated by the minister. Fortunately, the minister after examining the facts of the case, gave instructions that -these -pilots be reinstated. Nevertheless, the superintendent of pilots was under the impression, when the suspensions took place, that he was the pilotage authority. That is exactly why this amendment to the act is moved this evening, i-t is -to avoid a similar occurrence in the future. After a pilot is dismissed or suspended by an official of the Department of Marine, what recourse will we have, if this amendment is adopted? The minister will then reply that the pilotage authority had made such and such a decision, I am helpless.
I contend that such powers should be vested in the minister or deputy -minister only.
The minister may delegate such powers and appoint a competent official. Pilots who do not wish to carry out special duties, will be ;6uspended, and this will only be fair and just.
I have heard the amendment read once, but I have not heard the amendment as amended. Would you mind reading it now as amended, Mr. Chairman?

It now reads as follows:
Whenever the minister is appointed as pilotage authority for any district, his successors in office or any acting minister or, in the absence of the minister, his lawful deputy, shall be the pilotage authority, and any such pilotage authority may by by-law confirmed by the governor in council, authorize the superintendent of pilots in the district to exercise any of his functions, and for such time or such purpose as he may decide, authorize any person to exercise any particular function or power vested in the pilotage authority by this act or any by-law made hereunder.
Is the authority to be granted to the original -minister's deputy or the second minister's deputy?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext:
His lawful deputy.
Mr. NElILL: Both ministers have lawful deputies. I want to know which deputy is referred to.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: It is the lawful deputy of the Minister of Marine.
There is no deputy minister of marine.

The deputy of the present minister. A good many of these references will aipply to the port of Vancouver. May I ask the minister if any request has been made for this legislation from any of the pilotage boards of British Columbia?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: No, we have had no such requests. It is purely an administrative amendment.
Has the minister any reason -to believe that this legislation will be acceptable?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: Oh, surely.
We have not heard anything to that effect.

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: To the amendment as drafted I do not think there would be any objection.

But the minister has no knowledge on the subject. The pilotage boards have not asked for it. How does the minister know that this legislation will be acceptable or workable to the pilotage boards of British Columbia?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: This does not affect any pilotage board; it affects only the pilots. If there is any place where we need delegation of power it is a place three thousand miles from Ottawa. It is that I may delegate my authority to hold an inquiry in Vancouver, for instance, otherwise I would have to go there myself.
The whole purpose of this amendment, then, is to authorize the minister to delegate his power?

speakerposition: Minister of Fisheries; Minister of Marine
speechtext: Exactly.

Amendment agreed to.
